_meta.description: Master index of all data files in the graphicsForADHD project. Each entry documents the file's source, schema, and which components consume it.
_meta.notes: data.ts imports the 7 API-sourced JSON files and exports derived maps/functions. Components import from data.ts, not directly from JSON.

worldbank_indicators.json.fetched_via: World Bank API v2, no auth required
worldbank_indicators.json.format: JSON object with named indicator arrays

row_schema.country_code: ISO-3166-1 alpha-3 (includes World Bank aggregates like AFE, WLD)

worldbank_indicators.json.aggregates: Contains World Bank region/income aggregates (AFE, WLD, etc.) — data.ts filters these out via isCountryCode()
data_ts_exports: gdpLatestRows — latest year row per country
consumed_by: EconomicSnapshot.svelte — gdpPerCapita, povertyRate, giniIndex, populationData, gdpLatestRows, countryName

who_health_indicators.json.fetched_via: WHO GHO API, no auth required
who_health_indicators.json.format: JSON object with named indicator arrays

row_schema.sex: SEX_BTSX (both sexes combined), SEX_MLE, SEX_FLE — data.ts filters for SEX_BTSX

data_ts_exports: depressionData — latest SEX_BTSX row per country
anxietyData — latest SEX_BTSX row per country
schizophreniaData — latest SEX_BTSX row per country
eatingDisordersData — latest SEX_BTSX row per country
alcoholData — latest SEX_BTSX row per country
drugsData — latest SEX_BTSX row per country
mentalHealthByCountry — Map<iso3, {depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating, alcohol, drugs}>
consumed_by: MentalHealthWorldMap.svelte — depressionData, anxietyData, schizophreniaData, eatingDisordersData, alcoholData, drugsData, mentalHealthByCountry, countryName

world_happiness_report_2026.json.format: JSON object with a single key containing an array of yearly rows
data_ts_exports: happinessData — all rows with simplified field names
happinessLatest — latest year only, sorted by rank

undp_hdi.json.format: JSON object with key 'Table 1' containing HDI rankings

row_schema.Table 1. Human Development Index and its: Country name or tier header (e.g. 'VERY HIGH HUMAN DEVELOPMENT')

data_ts_exports: hdiData — array of {rank, country, hdi, lifeExp, expectedSchooling, meanSchooling, gni}

transparency_cpi_2024.json.source: World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators (https://www.worldbank.org/en/publication/worldwide-governance-indicators — official wgidataset.xlsx, Estimate values)
transparency_cpi_2024.json.fetched_via: Downloaded wgidataset.xlsx and extracted per-country Estimate values per year (see /tmp/build_wgi.py pattern)
transparency_cpi_2024.json.format: JSON object with named indicator arrays

row_schema.year: String year (1996-2022; data.ts uses latest available via govYear)

transparency_cpi_2024.json.note: Replaces Transparency International CPI which was unavailable. Governance indicators serve as proxy for institutional quality/corruption.
data_ts_exports: govYear — latest available year in the file
govIndicators — object with Map<iso3, number> for each of the 6 indicators (filtered to govYear)
consumed_by: GovernanceRadar.svelte — govIndicators, govCountryNames, govYear (ECharts radar, min -2.5 / max 2.5)

data_ts_exports: prisonData — filtered to rows with rate > 0

education_indicators.json.fetched_via: World Bank API v2, no auth required
education_indicators.json.format: JSON object with named indicator arrays
data_ts_exports: educationData — object with Map<iso3, number> for pupilTeacherPrimary, pupilTeacherSecondary, tertiaryEnrollment, primaryEnrollment

wmh_10_country_adult_adhd_prevalence.jso.source: WHO World Mental Health Survey Initiative — Fayyad et al. 2007, British Journal of Psychiatry
wmh_10_country_adult_adhd_prevalence.jso.description: Adult ADHD prevalence (ages 18-44) across 10 countries using DSM-IV/CIDI diagnostic criteria

key_stats.higher_income_countries: 4.2% (Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, USA)

wmh_10_country_adult_adhd_prevalence.jso.note: This is the 10-country subset. The full 20-country study is paywalled — see wmh_20_country_adult_adhd_access_notes.json
wmh_10_country_adult_adhd_prevalence.jso.consumed_by: Not directly imported by components; used as reference data for narrative/research context

wmh_20_country_adult_adhd_access_notes.j.source: Documentation of paywalled 20-country WMH study (Fayyad et al. 2017, Springer) + Lara et al. 2009 (PMC open access)
wmh_20_country_adult_adhd_access_notes.j.description: Access barriers documentation and extracted data from abstracts for the full 20-country WMH adult ADHD study
wmh_20_country_adult_adhd_access_notes.j.format: JSON object with access notes and extracted statistics
data_gaps: Workplace impact data blocked by ResearchGate 403
wmh_20_country_adult_adhd_access_notes.j.consumed_by: Reference data only; not imported by components

adhd_comorbidities_research.json.source: Multiple peer-reviewed meta-analyses (Fazel 2024, Young 2014, Ginsberg 2010, van Emmerik 2012, Rohner 2023, Moldekleiv 2025, Garas 2025, Zahid 2020, ABCD 2025)
adhd_comorbidities_research.json.description: Structured statistics on ADHD comorbidities: prison populations, substance use disorders, depression, and suicide risk

sections.prison_populations: ADHD prevalence in prisons (8.3%-40% depending on methodology)
sections.substance_use_disorder: ADHD-SUD comorbidity (21-23% of SUD patients have ADHD; 4-5x hazard ratios)
sections.depression_and_suicide: ADHD-depression link (OR=3.34 suicidal behavior; 16% ADHD in hospitalized depressed adolescents)

adhd_comorbidities_research.json.consumed_by: Reference data for research context; not directly imported by components

china_vs_worldwide.json.source: Gao et al. 2025, Frontiers in Psychiatry (GBD 1990-2021 comparative analysis)
china_vs_worldwide.json.description: China vs. global ADHD burden comparison — China's burden increasing while global burden decreasing
china_vs_worldwide.json.format: JSON object with incidence, prevalence, DALYs, and AAPC data
china_vs_worldwide.json.key_finding: China age-standardized incidence rose from 103.58 to 126.23/100k (1990-2021); global fell from 61.67 to 58.67/100k
china_vs_worldwide.json.consumed_by: Reference data for narrative context; not directly imported by components

adolescents_young_adults_10_24.json.source: Yuan et al. 2026, PLoS ONE (GBD 1990-2021, ages 10-24)
adolescents_young_adults_10_24.json.description: ADHD epidemiology for adolescents and young adults globally — all rates declining but absolute cases rising due to population growth
adolescents_young_adults_10_24.json.format: JSON object with global, regional, and country-level data
adolescents_young_adults_10_24.json.consumed_by: Reference data for research context; not directly imported by components

gbd_2019_adhd_global.json.source: Cortese et al. 2023, Molecular Psychiatry (GBD 2019 re-analysis)
gbd_2019_adhd_global.json.description: Global ADHD estimates across 204 countries, all ages — documents GBD's potential underestimation of prevalence
gbd_2019_adhd_global.json.format: JSON object with global and country-level estimates

key_stats.gbd_underestimation_note: Actual data: 5.41% vs GBD imputed: 2.68% in children

gbd_2019_adhd_global.json.consumed_by: Reference data; not directly imported by components

gbd_2021_global_adhd_under20.json.source: Cortese et al. 2026, Molecular Psychiatry (GBD 2021, under-20s)
gbd_2021_global_adhd_under20.json.description: Most up-to-date GBD ADHD estimates for under-20s across 204 countries (1990-2021)
gbd_2021_global_adhd_under20.json.format: JSON object with global, regional, and country-level data
gbd_2021_global_adhd_under20.json.consumed_by: Reference data; not directly imported by components

adhd_prevalence_sources_metadata.json.description: Catalog/index of all data files with completeness status, source URLs, and documented data gaps
adhd_prevalence_sources_metadata.json.format: JSON object serving as a project data inventory
data_gaps_documented: Adult-specific GBD data not directly available
adhd_prevalence_sources_metadata.json.key_insight: WMH survey data (3.4%) consistently shows higher adult ADHD rates than GBD modeled estimates (1.13%)
adhd_prevalence_sources_metadata.json.consumed_by: Developer reference only; not imported by any component

adhd_cognitive_neuroscience_research.jso.source: Research synthesis created for the project
adhd_cognitive_neuroscience_research.jso.description: Structured overview of ADHD cognitive neuroscience: deficits (well-established) and strengths (emerging evidence)
adhd_cognitive_neuroscience_research.jso.format: JSON object with two main sections

sections.deficits: Sustained attention, working memory, response inhibition, time perception, emotional regulation, task-switching, intra-individual variability
sections.strengths: Divergent thinking/creativity, hyperfocus, novelty/reward-seeking, improvisation under pressure

adhd_cognitive_neuroscience_research.jso.honest_caveat: Deficit literature is far more rigorous (decades of controlled lab tasks) than strengths literature (newer, often self-report based)
adhd_cognitive_neuroscience_research.jso.consumed_by: Reference data for narrative/research context; not directly imported by components

adhd_cognitive_neuroscience_research.md.description: Essay-format synthesis of ADHD cognitive neuroscience — suitable for direct inclusion in documents or presentations
adhd_cognitive_neuroscience_research.md.consumed_by: Content source for narrative text; not imported by components

problem-for-others.md.description: Honest examination of how unmanaged adult ADHD affects household members, parents, romantic partners, and friends
problem-for-others.md.core_thesis: People around the ADHDer absorb the consequences of their executive dysfunction; treatment dramatically changes this
problem-for-others.md.consumed_by: Content source for narrative text; not imported by components

section-01-k-mero-khuskidai-xa.md.description: Section 1: First-person monologue about ADHD medication availability in Nepal — why it is mass-produced globally yet restricted locally
section-01-k-mero-khuskidai-xa.md.consumed_by: Script content for spoken-word presentation; not imported by components

section-02-chasma.md.description: Section 2: Extended metaphor/parable comparing ADHD diagnosis to the introduction of eyeglasses — 'For eyes, it's not like that anymore. But for mental health — it's still the same.'
section-02-chasma.md.consumed_by: Script content for spoken-word presentation; not imported by components

section-03-metagnosis.md.description: Section 3: Defines 'metagnosis' — the moment you realize you've lived your entire life with an undiagnosed condition. Multiple vignettes (dyslexia, ADHD, learning disability).
section-03-metagnosis.md.consumed_by: Script content for spoken-word presentation; not imported by components

section-04-problem-in-adhd.md.description: Section 4: Explains ADHD neurochemistry in accessible Nepali — dopamine (motivation, focus, impulse control) and norepinephrine (alertness, filtering). Concludes: 'This is not a character issue. This is a chemistry issue.'
section-04-problem-in-adhd.md.consumed_by: Script content for spoken-word presentation; not imported by components

finalADHD.md.description: Finalized script for spoken-word presentation on ADHD medication access in Nepal — references DDCA amphetamine ban and calls for legal reform
finalADHD.md.consumed_by: Script content for spoken-word presentation; not imported by components

rough_draft.md.description: Early draft of spoken-word monologue — personal narrative about ADHD, executive dysfunction, and stigma
rough_draft.md.consumed_by: Script content for spoken-word presentation; not imported by components

image_keywords.json.description: Search keywords and AI image generation prompts for visuals matched to script sections — intended for Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay, or AI image tools
image_keywords.json.format: JSON object with image entries containing section, timestamp_hint, keywords, and description
image_keywords.json.consumed_by: Reference data for visual asset generation; not imported by components

sud_by_sex.json.source: Moldekleiv et al. 2025, Norwegian cohort (ages 18-31, n=49,815 ADHD)
sud_by_sex.json.description: SUD prevalence in ADHD by sex with hazard ratios per substance type
sud_by_sex.json.format: JSON object with cohort meta + categories array (name, male_pct, female_pct, hr_male, hr_female)
consumed_by: SexDiffSUD.svelte — grouped ECharts bar, HR shown in axis labels + tooltip

comorbidities.json.source: Ginsberg et al. 2010, high-security Swedish prison (30 confirmed ADHD cases)
comorbidities.json.description: Psychiatric comorbidity percentages in prison ADHD cases
comorbidities.json.format: JSON object with study meta + comorbidities array (name, percent)
consumed_by: ComorbidityBreakdown.svelte — horizontal ECharts bar with value-mapped opacity

sud_by_substance.json.source: Rohner et al. 2023 meta-analysis (n=12,524 across 31 studies)
sud_by_substance.json.description: ADHD prevalence in SUD patients by substance type, with 95% CIs and overall pooled estimate
sud_by_substance.json.format: JSON object with meta_analysis + overall + substances array (name, percent, ci_low, ci_high, n_studies)
consumed_by: SUDbySubstance.svelte — ECharts bar + custom CI whisker series + overall markLine

prison_adhd_studies.json.description: ADHD prevalence in prison populations across studies vs general population baseline
prison_adhd_studies.json.format: JSON object with general_population_pct + studies array (name, prevalence, ci_low/ci_high nullable, n, note)
consumed_by: PrisonPrevalence.svelte — ECharts bar + custom CI whisker series + general-pop markLine

sdi_regions.json.source: GBD 2021 under-20 estimates (Cortese et al. 2026) + regional breakdowns
sdi_regions.json.description: SDI vs ADHD prevalence by region
sdi_regions.json.format: JSON object with regions array (region, sdi, prevalence_pct)
consumed_by: SDIScatter.svelte — ECharts scatter with region labels
